chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Hal-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Sa'ee (walking) between As-Safa and Al-Marwa upon the animal. He said: 'Yes, and upon the carriage.'

key_terms.الدَّابَّةِ: Ad-Dabbah: An animal used for riding (e.g., camel, horse)
key_terms.السَّعْيِ: Sa'ee: The ritual walking between the hills of Safa and Marwa
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa: One of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed
key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: Al-Mahmal: A carriage, palanquin, or seat carried by an animal
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa: The second hill in the Sa'ee ritual

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa while riding a camel or in a carriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Sa'ee ritual by permitting pilgrims to perform it while riding a mount or seated in a carriage (mahmal), accommodating those with physical limitations or the elderly. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (yusr) in ritual obligations, ensuring that the physical demands of Hajj do not become an undue burden. The permissibility extends beyond walking, reflecting the broader Islamic legal maxim that difficulty begets facilitation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Sa’ee performed  between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa upon the animal. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and upon the carriage’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who performs Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah riding on a stumper. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so as well as on a carriage.’”
